To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
a plant protein involved in disease resistance, the polygalac-turonase-inhibitor protein, was crystallized.
we have determined the structure of PGIP-2, a leucine-rich-repeat protein from Phaseolulus vulgaris that inhibits fungal polygalacturonases.
the protein has a molecular weight of approximately 50 kDa, and that the crystals diffract well and have a high solvent content.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the structure of the plant polygalacturonases (PGs), which are extracellular enzymes produced by a variety of pathogenic organisms.
the molecular basis of resistance to pathogens in plants.
the structural analysis of plant defence proteins and the elucidation of the mechanisms of action of these proteins.

the crystals are suitable for a structure determination at 2.3-2.5 A resolution.
the crystals of the polygalactuonase-inhibiting-protein (PGIP- 1) from Phaseo1us vulgaris diffracted to at least 1.8 A resolution.
the crystals of PGIP-2 are of good quality, diffract to 3.0A and belong to space group P2(1) with unit-cell parameters a = 43.2, b = 53.3, c = 54.6 A, beta = 93.5 degrees.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
PGIP-1 crystallizes as a homodimer, with a dimer interface formed by the leucine-rich repeats.
the protein crystallizes in a space group that is not consistent with the crystallography literature for other leucine-rich proteins, but is consistent with a model for the structure of the protein.
we have obtained a high-quality crystal of PGIP- 1 that has diffracted to 2.3-A resolution, and that we have determined the crystal structure of PGIP-2, which diffracted to a resolution of 2.4 A.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we can crystallize a protein that has a high content of leucine-rich repeats and that the crystals diffract well.
we were able to obtain crystals of a protein that was difficult to crystallize.
